post.caption: Fake pearls were made from fish scales. Around 1656, a Paris rosary maker named Jaquin began using them. The silvery liquid, called essence of the East, was ground from the scales of a small fish, the bleak. About 2,000 fish gave one liter. Its shine comes from a crystal called guanine. Makers coated hollow glass beads on the inside with it, then filled each bead with wax for strength. Majorica, in Spain, still coats glass beads with fish scale essence. Engineer Eduard Hugo Heusch founded it in Barcelona in 1890, and its factory now stands in Manacor, on Mallorca.
